research_level: highest-level taxonomy used for ranking, annotation, and evaluation
construct_origin: Researcher-defined from practical analytics recruitment work in an analytics recruiting platform function at ByteDance; ESCO is used as external calibration evidence rather than as the source of the five constructs.
global_rules: Classify substantive work purpose and content, not title, seniority, tenure, grade, reporting line, IC/manager/POC status, or team size.
A manager, consultant, freelancer, or external provider qualifies only through the concrete analytical work performed.
An isolated title, tool, or skill keyword is insufficient evidence for a Role Profile.
The five Role Profiles are project-specific research constructs and are not ByteDance's official job architecture or a comprehensive labour-market taxonomy.
The retired career-direction layer and prototype layer are not research constructs.

skill_evidence.scope_note: Candidate skills are frozen with the current candidate dataset. Role-level project-custom skills and ESCO occupation skills are governed separately.

aggregation_rule.scope_note: Occupation-to-Role-Profile aggregation must be selected on development data and frozen separately.

role_profiles.definition: Evaluates long-term internal and external change, emerging opportunities, risks, and strategic alternatives to support direction setting and resource allocation at group or business level, usually over a three-to-five-year horizon.
role_profiles.primary_purpose: Long-horizon direction setting and resource-allocation judgement.
core_task_areas: Analyse macroeconomic, industry, technology, regulatory, customer, and competitive developments.
Assess internal capabilities, portfolio position, and long-term business-performance drivers.
Identify emerging markets, new business opportunities, structural risks, and discontinuities.
Conduct market sizing, scenario analysis, and long-range forecasting.
Compare strategic options and their resource implications.
Produce long-horizon strategic reports and recommendations for group-level or business-level decision makers.
candidate_evidence: Evidence of analysing broad external and internal change beyond current operating performance.
A multi-year horizon, normally three to five years, or equivalent long-range reasoning.
Comparison of strategic alternatives, opportunities, or risks.
Implications for direction, portfolio choices, capabilities, investment, or resource allocation.
include_when: The central purpose is long-term strategic judgement at group, business, product-area, or market level.
The work substantively examines both external change and internal capability or position.
Outputs include strategic options, long-range analysis, opportunity assessment, or resource-allocation recommendations.
The analytical horizon extends beyond routine operating cycles and short-term issue resolution.
exclude_when: The central work is administrative implementation or coordination of an already determined strategy.
The work primarily monitors short-term targets, budgets, or routine operating performance.
The work is limited to marketing research without broader strategic interpretation.
The work is primarily academic economics or public-policy research without organisation- or business-level strategy application.
The work mainly delivers process, ICT, or operational improvement rather than long-term direction setting.
boundary_notes: Strategic Analysis differs from Business Strategy & Focused Analysis through its broader scope, longer horizon, external-change evidence, strategic alternatives, and resource-allocation implications.

Strategic Analysis evidence may transfer to Focused Analysis when it also demonstrates concrete problem decomposition and actionable recommendations; the reverse transfer requires explicit long-horizon evidence.
Both group-level and business-level Strategic Analysis are included.

role_profiles.definition: Translates business objectives into measurable targets, monitors performance, explains variances, and supports recurring planning, budgeting, forecasting, and business-review cycles.
role_profiles.primary_purpose: Maintain an ongoing management loop between goals, evidence, diagnosis, and corrective action.
core_task_areas: Decompose business goals and define performance measures.
Design and maintain KPI and performance-management frameworks.
Support budgeting, rolling forecasts, and operating plans.
Compare actual performance with targets, budgets, or prior periods.
Diagnose performance variance and business drivers.
Prepare recurring business reviews and follow up improvement actions.
candidate_evidence: Ownership or substantive contribution to goals, KPIs, budgets, forecasts, or operating plans.
Explanation of variance and underlying business drivers rather than production of figures alone.
A recurring review cadence that links findings to management decisions or corrective action.
Business-side decision support rather than accounting control, compliance, or financial administration.
include_when: Recurring business-performance management is a central purpose.
The work substantively uses goals, KPIs, budgets, forecasts, variance, or business reviews.
The role explains performance rather than only producing figures.
Outputs feed recurring management and operating decisions.
exclude_when: Forecasting primarily concerns inventory, supply-chain demand, or production scheduling.
The work is mainly accounting, audit, financial compliance, investment analysis, pure financial management, or budget-policy administration.
The role only produces reports or dashboards without performance interpretation and action follow-up.
The role mainly addresses one-off strategic or commercial questions.
The role primarily determines long-term corporate or business direction.
boundary_notes: The recurring goal-to-review-to-action loop distinguishes this profile from one-off Business Strategy & Focused Analysis.
Finance-BP-like work is included only where it supports a concrete business's planning and performance decisions; pure finance management is excluded.
Data Analytics may provide KPI and variance evidence, but does not qualify unless the work owns or substantively supports the recurring performance-management loop.

role_profiles.definition: Structures ambiguous and non-routine business questions, combines quantitative and qualitative evidence, compares alternatives, and produces actionable recommendations for specific growth, product, customer, commercial, process, or operating decisions.
role_profiles.primary_purpose: Resolve a bounded business question through structured diagnosis, option comparison, and actionable recommendations.
core_task_areas: Define and decompose ambiguous business problems.
Develop analytical hypotheses and issue frameworks.
Conduct focused quantitative analysis and business diagnosis.
Gather qualitative evidence through interviews, desk research, or cross-functional consultation.
Compare business cases, alternatives, costs, benefits, and likely impacts.
Formulate and communicate actionable recommendations.
candidate_evidence: A concrete enterprise or business question with a defined decision context.
Structured problem framing or hypothesis development.
Use of quantitative and/or qualitative evidence to compare alternatives.
A business case, strategic response, pilot, improvement path, or actionable recommendation.
include_when: Structuring business problems and producing recommendations are central purposes.
The work combines business understanding with quantitative or qualitative evidence.
The work addresses varied, non-routine questions rather than a single recurring reporting process.
Outputs include a business case, strategic response, decision option, or improvement path.
exclude_when: The central work is ICT requirements capture, system design, or technical implementation.
The work primarily operates routine KPI, planning, or business-review cycles.
The work mainly studies long-term corporate or business direction and broad structural change.
The work primarily produces data pipelines, dashboards, or statistical models.
The work provides generic advisory services without substantive analytical problem solving.
boundary_notes: This profile examines a focused topic or bounded decision; it is not defined by being informal or merely ad hoc.
A Strategic Analysis practitioner may have transferable evidence for this profile, but a focused analyst does not automatically qualify for Strategic Analysis without explicit long-horizon evidence.
Consultant, freelancer, or external-provider work counts only when grounded in a concrete enterprise and business problem with substantive analytical outputs.

role_profiles.definition: Converts raw data into reliable, interpretable, and reusable evidence for recurring business decisions through data preparation, metric-system design, analytical data foundations, reporting, visualisation, and descriptive or diagnostic analysis.
role_profiles.primary_purpose: Create trustworthy and reusable business-side measurement and diagnostic evidence.
core_task_areas: Acquire, clean, transform, validate, and reconcile data.
Design metric systems, definitions, dimensions, and calculation standards.
Develop or maintain reusable analytical datasets, data marts, semantic layers, and data dictionaries.
Define data-quality checks and support analytics-oriented data governance.
Query and analyse data using tools such as SQL.
Build reports, dashboards, and visualisations.
Conduct descriptive and diagnostic analysis and communicate findings to business stakeholders.
candidate_evidence: Hands-on evidence of data preparation, validation, reconciliation, or querying.
Metric definitions, dimensions, governed datasets, semantic layers, dashboards, or reusable analytical assets.
Descriptive or diagnostic analysis tied to a concrete business decision.
Communication of findings to business stakeholders.
include_when: Data preparation and analysis are central rather than incidental activities.
Outputs include governed metrics, reusable analytical data assets, reports, dashboards, visualisations, or diagnostic insights.
The work contributes to the reliability and repeatability of analytical evidence.
The primary decision contribution is descriptive or diagnostic rather than model-driven prediction or optimisation.
exclude_when: The primary output is a machine-learning, predictive, causal, recommendation, or optimisation model.

The work primarily engineers low-level data platforms, distributed systems, storage infrastructure, warehouses, data-quality governance, or production pipelines without substantial business-side analytical ownership.
Data analysis is only an auxiliary skill within another occupation.
The central responsibility is goal management, budgeting, or business-performance review.
The principal work is database administration or software engineering.
boundary_notes: Metric systems and analytics-oriented data foundations are included, but dedicated warehouse, platform, data-quality, and infrastructure occupations are excluded.
Business-side diagnostic work distinguishes this profile from low-level data engineering.
Data Science is distinguished by models, experiments, causal inference, prediction, recommendation, or optimisation as central outputs.

role_profiles.definition: Uses statistical modelling, machine learning, experimentation, causal inference, and optimisation to build and evaluate predictive or decision-support models from data.
role_profiles.primary_purpose: Produce and evaluate model- or experiment-based evidence for prediction, causal judgement, recommendation, or optimisation.
core_task_areas: Conduct exploratory analysis and prepare modelling data.
Perform feature engineering and model selection.
Build predictive, classification, recommendation, causal, or optimisation models.
Design and analyse A/B tests, randomised experiments, multivariate experiments, quasi-experiments, and uplift analyses.
Train, validate, compare, and monitor models.
Interpret model and experiment results.
Communicate how model or experimental evidence should inform decisions.
candidate_evidence: Model or experiment design tied to a concrete product, operational, or business decision.
Feature engineering, model selection, baseline comparison, validation, calibration, sensitivity analysis, or monitoring.
A/B testing, randomised or quasi-experimental analysis, causal inference, heterogeneous-effect analysis, or uplift modelling.
Interpretation of model or experiment results and their decision implications.
include_when: Statistical or machine-learning models, experiments, causal methods, or optimisation methods are central work products.
The occupation substantively involves model construction and evaluation.
The work estimates effects or uses models for prediction, classification, recommendation, or optimisation.
The work goes beyond describing historical data to produce generalisable model- or experiment-based evidence.
exclude_when: The primary work is routine reporting, dashboarding, metric monitoring, or descriptive analysis.
The work uses only basic statistics to summarise business performance.
The work primarily develops data infrastructure, databases, production pipelines, or general software systems.
The work is purely theoretical or academic statistical research without an applied modelling, experimentation, or decision context.
Modelling is only an incidental skill rather than a central output.
boundary_notes: A/B testing and other controlled or quasi-experimental work are core Data Science evidence in this project.
Data Analytics is descriptive/diagnostic and reusable-measurement oriented; Data Science is model-, experiment-, causal-, prediction-, recommendation-, or optimisation-oriented.
AI engineering is supporting rather than core when engineering intelligent systems dominates the analytical model-and-decision lifecycle.
